newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish telecoms deregulation bill delayed.
newsitem.headline: Danish telecoms deregulation bill delayed.

text.p: Denmark's government said on Thursday that talks with opposition parties on final legislation deregulating the telecommunications industry broke down and would probably not be completed until autumn at the earliest.
"We are unable to complete our negotiations in time to meet the July deadline," Research Minister Jytte Hilden told Reuters after the talks collapsed.
"It looks like the deregulation of the telecoms industry in Denmark cannot be carried out now until the autumn or early next year," she said.
The Danish telecommunications industry was largely deregulated on July 1, 1996 with a final phase of enabling legislation due for passage by parliament this spring.
The former monopoly operator Tele Danmark, which is 51.73 owned by the state and the market leader, had complained that the legislation would cut its earnings.

The company was particularly irked by government plans to price-cap interconnect access to Tele Danmark's network by competitors which it claimed would mean unreasonably low charges in a cut throat market.

On Tuesday Tele Danmark posted 1996 results showing a pre-tax profit of 5.067 billion crowns, down from 1995's 5.458 billion crowns and warned that the liberalisation meant growing competition and further market share losses in the area of telephony.

The telecoms negotiations between the Social Democrat-led minority government and opposition parties broke down over whether the deregulation bill should embrace the entire market or mobile telephony should come under separate legislation. --Morten Bonde Petersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
